full_judgment:
3. Plaint case, in short, is that the entire land of S.S. plot No. 229 appertaining to D.P. Khatian No. 444 originally belonged to Gour Singha. During the last settlement operation the said land was correctly recorded in his name. By a registered sale deed dated 03.04.61 Gour Singha transferred the suit land to Md. Riasat Ali and delivered him possession. In 1971 when Riasat Ali was killed by the Muktifoul, his father Ejabat Ali, widow Mrs. Jamila Khatoon alias Mrs. Jamuna Riasat, son Kemal Ahmed alias Rinku and one daughter Miss Koli inherited and possessed the suit land. 

 6. After purchase, the plaintiff came to know that though the record of rights was prepared in the name of Gour Singha in D.P. Khatian but name of one Abdul Hasib was also recorded in the printed Khatian. Being approached, said Abdul Hasib gave up all his interest in the suit land by a registered deed of `muktipatra' dated 18.02.81. Plaintiff then got her name mutated in Mutation Case No. 2350/1980-80 and since possessed on payment of rent on proper receipts. 

 21. In cross-examination, he stated that he did not see Gour Singha. He also did not see Riasat Ali in purchasing the suit land. He also did not know Monmoy Purakaysta. Monmoy wrote the deed of Riasat Ali. he knew D.W.1 Upendra Singha and D.W.2 Chandra Singha who are the identified of the executant and witness to the deed respectively. He did not see Riasat Ali possessing the suit land but he saw Ejabat Ali possessing the suit land. He was present when Shamsul Hussain Chowdhury and Abdul Ahad Chowdhury got the deed. He was present at the time of delivery of possession to the plaintiff. He lived in a house away from the suit land. He heard Gour Singha died in 1968. He knew the suit land since 1970. After purchase, having gone for mutation he became aware of the khatian. On 22.10.83 defendant No. 1 to 4 along with the goons dispossessed them. He could not recognize the goons.
